findings: S7 sibling-family collection (lines 131-137) is a no-op: FileRepository package entries are directories (name pattern qcd*8380.inf_arm64_*), but `Where-Object { -not $_.PSIsContainer }` (line 133) filters OUT directories, so no adjacent-family INF/CAT is ever copied - opposite of the section comment's stated intent. (C3, C6)

Files matching *.ini and secondary INFs (e.g. qcdx8380umd.inf) are never collected explicitly anywhere; only the newest package's full copy in S6 could incidentally include them, so 'INF/CAT/INI of ALL versions' is only partially true. (C3)

Line 97 hard-codes `-Encoding Unicode` for qcdx8380.inf. If the DriverStore INF is ANSI, the DriverVer regex fails, Version becomes $null, and S6's 'newest package' selection (line 110) can pick an arbitrary package (and lose the version manifest). Encoding assumption is unverified for this exact INF. (C6)

S7 firmware copies (lines 126-127) are non-recursive: *.mbn and qcdxkmbase*.bin are only taken from each package's root, so firmware in subdirectories of older packages is missed (newest package is still fully covered by S6). (C3 minor)

Line 184 uses `/ow:$true`, which PowerShell expands to `/ow:True`; wevtutil documents lowercase true|false. If rejected, the .evtx export silently fails (stderr to $null, stdout Out-Null) and no .evtx files are produced. Unverified case-sensitivity. (C6 minor)

Line 154 filters Enum\ACPI children on '^VEN_QCOM'; if the Adreno instance enumerates as 'QCOMxxxx' (common on ARM ACPI), the ACPI enum exports match nothing. Device-dependent, low confidence, but should likely be '^(VEN_QCOM|QCOM)'. (C3 minor)

Compress-Archive (line 233) runs while Start-Transcript still holds transcript.log open; PS 5.1 can fail with file-in-use on locked files. The catch logs it and keeps the raw folder, but the zip may be lost on every run. (C4/C6 minor)

A failed [version] cast (line 99) aborts the entire S5 try block, so package-manifest.json is lost for all packages when one INF parses badly. Caught and logged, but per-package resilience would be better. (C4/C6 minor)
